context: Interactive CPU profile flame chart showing ~855 synthetic stack frames across 8 modules (core, http, database, auth, cache, logging, scheduler, io), rendered on canvas with zoom/pan and click-to-drill-down.
first_impression: Core encoding is honest — d3.partition correctly allocates width proportional to CPU time — but two hardcoded magic numbers (domain [0,10000] and tooltip divisor /10000) would silently break under data changes.
what_works: Width encoding via d3.partition is mathematically correct: space is allocated proportionally to aggregated self_time, and zoom applies linear scaling (x0*k+tx) that preserves proportions; canvas LOD rendering avoids D3 join key-function issues entirely since every draw is a full re-render.
what_doesnt: timeScale.domain([0, 10000]) is a hardcoded magic number instead of data-driven (should be root.data.total_time), and tooltip percentage calculations divide by 10000 — both break the Scaling metamorphic relation if total profiling time changes; additionally d3.partition sorts children by aggregated value rather than preserving temporal call order, which is atypical for flame charts and can misrepresent call sequence.
